data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 14 out of 18 financial companies beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
Financial companies remained in the spotlight this week as investors digested quarterly results from the largest payment companies, insurers, exchanges, brokers, and asset managers.

Major names including JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), Citigroup (C), Wells Fargo (WFC), Goldman Sachs (GS), Bank of America (BAC), Morgan Stanley (MS), and BlackRock (BLK) reported earnings during the week.

The Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) gained 0.7% over the past week, compared with a 2% decline in the S&P 500 (SP500). On a YTD basis, XLF has underperformed the broader market with 0.8% returns, while the S&P 500 has gained nearly 12%.

Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line (EPS): Out of 18 financial companies that reported earnings this week, 14 beat analysts' estimates, three missed, and one reported in line with expectations.

Top Line (Revenue): 11 companies beat revenue estimates, while seven missed.

Below are some of the key companies that reported earnings this week:

The U.S.'s largest bank by assets, JPMorgan Chase's Q3 earnings and revenue missed Wall Street consensus estimates. Its Q3 commercial and investment banking results softened markedly from Q2's robust pace. Each line of business, though, grew from the year-ago quarter.

Citigroup (C) Q3 earnings exceeded the Wall Street consensus as its services and wealth units posted solid gains after markets and investment banking revenue weakened from the previous quarter. The lender now expects full-year 2026 net interest income, ex-markets, to rise in the mid-to-high 6% range from 2025’s $49.8B, compared with its prior guidance of ~5%-6%.

Wells Fargo (WFC) capital market revenues fell short of expectations during the third quarter, impacting overall revenue at the San Francisco-based bank. For the fourth quarter, NII is expected to be ~$13B, vs. $12.82B consensus.

Goldman Sachs (GS) Q3 top and bottom lines exceeded consensus estimates even as markets-related revenue eased from an unusually strong Q2. Solid growth in its asset and wealth management business helped to offset the less hectic market activity in Q3.

Bank of America (BAC) reported Q3 diluted EPS of $0.91, down from $1.04 a year earlier and below the $1.09 consensus estimate. Results were impacted by a $1.2 billion U.S. Treasury fine for anti-money laundering and sanctions violations, which reduced EPS by $0.17.

BlackRock (BLK) reported its Q3 results, beating Wall Street earnings and revenue expectations across the board.

Overall, financial sector earnings were resilient this week. About 78% of reported companies beat EPS estimates, while 61% beat revenue expectations, showing that many companies continued to deliver solid profits despite mixed revenue growth.

Earnings next week

For the upcoming week, investors will continue to watch earnings from the financial sector, such as American Express (AXP), Blackstone (BX), Capital One Financial (COF), and Synchrony Financial (SYF).

data.title: Kennedy, White House officials to revive food policy talks next week: Politico
data.description:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is expected to meet with senior White House officials next week to discuss the status of U.S. food policy as part of a revived push to define ultra-processed foods, Politico reported on Saturday.

Discussions among officials have gathered pace over recent weeks after a pause this summer,  according to three Trump administration officials who were granted anonymity to disclose internal conversations.

Previously, Kennedy promised to get a definition for ultra-processed foods “by April” and follow up with a system for food grading in a move that could tighten regulation on packaged offerings such as chips and sodas.

In August, the HHS and the U.S. Department of Agriculture submitted the federal government’s first proposed definition of ultra-processed foods for final review as a white paper, which, however, fell short of being a legally enforceable rule.

The discussions come less than two weeks into the midterm elections amid calls by Kennedy and many members of his Make America Healthy Again movement to include warning labels for ultra-processed foods.

HHS didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

Potentially relevant tickers: PepsiCo (PEP), Kellanova (K), Kraft Heinz (KHC), McDonald's (MCD), Yum! Brands (YUM), Restaurant Brands International (QSR), Coca-Cola (KO), B&G Foods (BGS), Conagra Brands (CAG), Celsius (CELH), Hershey (HSY), Mondelez (MDLZ), and  Invesco Food & Beverage ETF (PBJ)

Dear readers, we recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: Notable analyst calls: Salesforce, Walmart and Lockheed Martin gain analyst support as tech downgrades mount
data.description:
Wall Street analysts issued a fresh round of upgrades and downgrades last week, with shifting views on AI’s impact on software, hardware makers’ growth prospects, and resilience to inflation. Salesforce (CRM) and Walmart (WMT) drew upgrades, while Adobe (ADBE) and several technology hardware stocks faced downgrades.

Salesforce upgraded by Bank of America on enterprise AI outlook

Salesforce (CRM) was upgraded to Buy from Underperform by Bank of America on October 12, with the brokerage raising its price target to $285 from $160. The firm said large enterprises are unlikely to replace software platforms that house their business logic, data, workflows and compliance frameworks as they adopt AI. Instead, AI adoption could deepen reliance on these systems.

The $285 price target values Salesforce (CRM) at 16 times its expected free cash flow for 2027, up from 9 times previously and above the peer average of 15 times. The brokerage cited easing concerns about AI-driven disruption, the company's AI strategy, strong free cash flow generation and the potential for revenue growth to accelerate.

Barclays downgrades Dell, HPE and NetApp as AI growth concerns mount

Dell Technologies (DELL), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and NetApp (NTAP) were downgraded to Equal Weight from Overweight by Barclays on October 14. Analyst Tim Long lowered Dell's (DELL) price target to $574 from $603 and HPE's (HPE) to $77 from $83, while maintaining NetApp's (NTAP) target at $219.

Barclays adopted a more cautious view of IT hardware companies exposed to enterprise spending, citing elevated valuations, revenue gains supported by higher memory prices and a lack of a meaningful AI-driven growth inflection.

HubSpot and monday.com downgraded by Barclays on delayed AI benefits

HubSpot (HUBS) and monday.com (MNDY) were downgraded to Equal Weight from Overweight by Barclays on October 12, as the brokerage said AI-related benefits could take longer to materialize than previously expected. 

Barclays maintained its price target of $240 for HubSpot (HUBS) and $100 for monday.com (MNDY). For HubSpot (HUBS), the firm said its bullish thesis had relied on AI usage accelerating growth, but customer caution during the AI transition could delay that improvement. For monday.com (MNDY), analyst Raimo Lenschow said AI monetization was gaining traction but remained in its early stages, with AI ARR accounting for only 1% of total ARR and not yet offsetting a slowdown in core growth.

Deutsche Bank upgrades Walmart as inflation bolsters value proposition

Walmart (WMT) was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Deutsche Bank on October 15, with analyst Krisztina Katai raising the price target to $136 from $113. The brokerage said persistent inflation could strengthen Walmart’s value proposition and accelerate market-share gains as consumers seek lower prices.

Deutsche Bank expects margin growth from advertising, marketplace, and membership, alongside automation gains. Strong food market-share gains and e-commerce momentum also support its improved 2027 outlook.

GoDaddy downgraded by RBC as AI reshapes the web

GoDaddy (GDDY) was downgraded to Sector Perform from Outperform by RBC Capital Markets on October 12. Analyst Brad Erickson maintained his $95 price target, citing the potential impact of AI agents on the company's traditional domain, website-building and digital-commerce businesses. 

RBC said the internet was shifting from static, publisher-driven pages toward AI agents that deliver results based on user intent. The brokerage also cited GoDaddy's (GDDY) 38% rebound from its June low, saying the rally left less room for further valuation expansion.

MongoDB stays bullish as Needham and BofA reaffirm Buy ratings

MongoDB (MDB) rose more than 6% on October 13 after Needham and Bank of America reiterated their Buy ratings on the database software company. Needham maintained its price target at $430, while BofA kept its target at $540. 

Needham analyst Mike Cikos said discussions following MongoDB's Investor Day reinforced the firm's confidence in the company's go-to-market strategy, platform cross-selling opportunities, and potential to expand adoption among large customers. Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda said MongoDB's (MDB) JSON document database remains differentiated for enterprise digital modernization and AI workloads, supporting the firm's long-term growth outlook. 

Wells Fargo double downgrades Adobe, upgrades Tyler Technologies

Adobe (ADBE) was downgraded to Underweight from Overweight by Wells Fargo on October 12, with analyst Michael Turrin cutting the price target to $225 from $270. The firm cited slowing organic growth, rising AI competition and execution risks amid a management transition. 

In contrast, Wells Fargo upgraded Tyler Technologies (TYL) to Overweight from Equal Weight and raised its price target to $400 from $335, citing fading booking headwinds and scope for a recovery in 2027. 

Well Fargo also raised its price targets on ServiceNow (NOW) to $190 from $175, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) to $525 from $475, and CrowdStrike (CRWD) to $300 from $235. It cut its target on Figma (FIG) to $30 from $34.

Vertical Research upgrades Lockheed Martin on missile demand

Lockheed Martin (LMT) was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Vertical Research on October 14, with analyst Robert Stallard setting a $600 price target. Stallard expects the company’s missile business to grow about 11% annually through the end of the decade, citing demand for missile replenishment despite uncertainty over the U.S. defense budget.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: CoreWeave, TSMC, Anthropic in focus
data.description:
Technology stocks slumped this week, with chipmakers and AI infrastructure providers leading losses as investors questioned the returns on heavy AI investments.

The Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) also came under pressure, falling more than 4% for the week, while the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) fell 7.20% over the week, reflecting broad weakness across the technology sector.

The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • Fair Isaac (FICO) +13.91%
  • Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH) +9.56%
  • Tyler Technologies (TYL) +8.55%
  • Accenture (ACN) +8.05%
  • Gartner (IT) +6.66%

Top Losers:

  • Ciena (CIEN) -25.14%
  • Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) -25.08%
  • Coherent (COHR) -24.62%
  • Super Micro Computer (SMCI) -24.44%
  • Lumentum (LITE) -24.21%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

CoreWeave sell-off puts AI infrastructure financing under scrutiny

CoreWeave (CRWV) shares plunged 12.80% on Friday as investors questioned the cost of expanding AI data centers. The sell-off spread to Nebius (NBIS) and IREN (IREN) amid concerns about borrowing costs and capital requirements.

CoreWeave's debt and lease obligations totaled approximately $52B at the end of June, highlighting the financial burden of its AI infrastructure expansion.

TSMC outlook signals resilient AI chip demand

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) forecasted fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3B to $54.3B, above analysts' consensus of $50.48B, providing fresh evidence of resilient semiconductor demand.

Third-quarter high-performance computing revenue rose 22% quarter over quarter. Management said AI accelerator revenue growth could exceed its previous mid-to-high-50% CAGR forecast for 2024–2029, signaling continued demand despite the broader technology sell-off.

Anthropic IPO valuation expectations cool as growth slows

Anthropic's (ANTHRO) anticipated initial public offering faces greater valuation scrutiny as investors assess its growth trajectory and AI development costs. 

Reuters reported that some investors were discussing a potential valuation of around $1.5T, below earlier expectations of approximately $2T.

The AI company reportedly generated $16.8B in third-quarter revenue, up 45% sequentially, and was profitable on an adjusted basis. However, the slower growth rate disappointed some investors after revenue more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6B in the second quarter. 

The valuation discussions remain preliminary and do not represent confirmed IPO pricing.

AI spending pressures hyperscaler cash flow

Bank of America Global Research expects Microsoft (MSFT) to be the only major hyperscaler among its comparison group not to enter negative free cash flow territory over the next 12 months. 

Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Oracle (ORCL), and Meta Platforms (META) are projected to face negative free cash flow as AI infrastructure investment continues. The firm expects cash generation to recover by the second half of 2027, assuming AI revenue accelerates and capital expenditure growth slows.

Bank of America sees memory-stock sell-off diverging from fundamentals

Bank of America analysts said the recent pullback in SK Hynix (SKHY) and Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) may reflect fears of an AI spending slowdown rather than weakening memory fundamentals. Investors have worried about borrowing costs for AI cloud providers, potential Chinese supply growth, and the sustainability of demand.

BofA, however, expects memory prices, sales, and margins to remain strong through 2028. The divergence highlights uncertainty around the memory cycle: shares have come under pressure even as some forecasts point to continued demand and earnings strength.

Meta expands open AI model push with Muse Spark Open

Meta Platforms (META) released Muse Spark Open, an AI model designed for coding and complex tasks. It has 816B parameters, with 42B active during use, and its weights are available to developers. The model can run locally on suitably configured Apple (AAPL) Mac Studio computers, expanding Meta's open-model offering.

data.title: Insurance stocks, TransUnion among winners; Banks, IREN in losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street closed the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 1.44% from the prior week to close at $55.52.

Among megacap financial stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD) was a notable gainer, adding 4.60% week-over-week to $120.39.

TD Bank was among the nine largest U.S. banks engaged in the so-called "debanking" activity, according to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's recent report.

The stock lost 0.27% on the day, but was rising for the remainder of the week. 

Mastercard (MA) (+4.80% W/W to $617.42) and Visa (V) (+4.45% W/W to $402.61) were the other major gainers. The two stocks have been gaining since the launch of Open USD (OPEN-USD) stablecoin last month.

Bank of America (BAC) led the decliners, having posted its worst day since April 2025 on Wednesday. The stock fell 5.69% week-over-week to $51.23.

The stock plunged after the U.S. Department of the Treasury imposed over $1.21B in penalties against the lender over anti-money laundering and sanctions laws violations. The regulatory fine impacted the bank's third-quarter profit.

Morgan Stanley's (MS) Q3 earnings exceeded expectations despite a weakness in fixed income and investment management. However, the stock underperformed with a 4.97% decline to $180.57.

Citigroup (C) followed with a 4.15% decrease to $124.26. Q3 earnings beat analyst estimates but saw sequential declines across investment banking, trading, and firm-wide profitability.

The KBW Nasdaq Bank Index (BKX) underperformed the broader markets, with investors split on how to read Q3 bank earnings, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

"One camp sees positive net interest income outlooks and strong returns and capital and consumer spend. The other sees rising deposits costs and [accumulated other comprehensive income] eating buybacks and concerns on lending standards and credit sustainability," said Truist Securities analyst Brian Foran.

Among largecap stocks, TransUnion (TRU) topped the advancers with a 13.13% addition to $74.08. The week saw TransUnion strike a deal with Bankrate to power more personalized credit offers for millions of consumers.

Additionally, a general strength was seen across the broader credit reporting sector.

IREN (IREN) (-23.30% W/W to $26.99) was the biggest loser despite the crypto miner-turned-AI server agreeing on a multiyear cloud deal with Anthropic.

The week saw most neocloud stocks fall after a report by Gartner predicted 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030 if AI infrastructure spending continues at its breakneck speed.

Pershing Square (PS) was the next on the list, retreating 18.52% to $44.48. The stock was downgraded at Citi and BofA Securities.

MARA Holdings (MARA) (-21.97% W/W to $7.53), Galaxy Digital (GLXY) (-20.61% W/W to $16.14), and CleanSpark (CLSK) (-19.96% W/W to $8.40) were among the top midcap decliners.

For the winners, insurance stocks RLI (RLI) (+9.62% W/W to $61.07), Kinsale Capital (KNSL) (+8.39% W/W to $365.24), Slide Insurance (SLDE) (+7.68% W/W to $27.07), and Hagerty (HGTY) (+7.67% W/W to $15.30). The sector was trading higher on the back of above-expected earnings posted by Travelers (TRV) and Marsh (MRSH).

American Coastal Insurance (ACIC) (+13.50% W/W to $11.10), Kemper (KMPR) (+8.61% W/W to $29.27), AGI (AGBK) (+8.58% W/W to $7.34), Bit Digital (BTBT) (-25.60% W/W to $0.96), and Bitgo Holdings (BTGO) (-19.78% W/W to $5.88) were the notable smallcap movers.

data.title: Semiconductor ETF posts longest losing streak in over two decades amid chip selloff
data.description:
iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed more than 4% lower on Friday, marking its ninth consecutive session of declines and capping its longest losing streak since May 2026 amid a broader selloff of chip stocks.

The fund, which tracks companies in the semiconductor sector, lost nearly 12% this week, its biggest weekly decline since April 2025, as all but two of the 34 constituents of the ETF ended in negative territory.

A selloff that began amid worries over the pace of AI buildout and credit concerns affecting CoreWeave (CRWV) deepened after the latest CPI report indicated a hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation, fueling fears over a more restrictive monetary policy from the Federal Reserve.

Applied Materials (AMAT), ASE Technology (ASX), SK Hynix (SKHY), Credo Technology (CRDO), and Teradyne (TER) all lost more than 15% to become the five biggest laggards of SOXX this week. NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), Microchip Technology (MCHP), QUALCOMM (QCOM), Texas Instruments (TXN), and Analog Devices (ADI) were among the top five outperformers.

data.title: Marvell and Nvidia outlooks provide buying opportunities during downturn: GF
data.description:
The current downturn among semiconductor stocks has created a buying opportunity for quality names, such as Nvidia (NVDA) and Marvell (MRVL), according to GF Securities.

GF analysts attended the OCP Global Summit in San Jose last week, which reflected a shift toward full-stack co-design across hyperscalers.

"Nvidia's networking roadmap now spans both co‑packaged optics and the new USFP pluggable standard, co‑developed with Cisco (CSCO) to raise density and serviceability inside AI factories," said GF analyst Jeff Pu in an investor report. "USFP modules deliver up to 12.8 Tb/s per module and 400 Gb/s per lane, achieving near‑CPO efficiency while retaining the flexibility of pluggables for field maintenance."

The USFP stands for ultra-dense small form factor pluggable and is a new optical transceiver standard used to connect massive AI data center clusters.

"Our U.S. tour to neoclouds suggests power availability and licensing remain decisive factors for expansion," Pu noted. "However, there is no power shortage issue by now and in the foreseeable future, as most sites located far from urban centers, and many use stable gas‑based generation. For electricity cost, regional cost spreads remain wide, driving migration of new builds toward the southern corridor and select overseas zones such as Italy. For shell, the modular datacenter shells can be completed in as little as three months, but liquid‑cooling infrastructure continues to be the bottleneck."

The tour also revealed the rising importance of CPU for inference, especially for agentic AI. This is expected to double the total addressable market for CPUs.

"GPU utilization for decode workloads averages only 20–30%, and SRAM‑based accelerators struggle with long‑context efficiency," Pu said. "Token costs are falling 5–10× every year, but semi and memory costs are rising. Bottlenecks are NAND, DRAM, and cooling. The agentic AI factory model—where orchestration and retrieval run on CPUs—reshapes unit economics: CPU‑to‑accelerator ratios move from 1:4–1:8 in chat‑era systems to 1:1 in agentic deployments."

"Despite the broad market softness, we suggest investors accumulate quality stocks," he added. "We continue to like Nvidia, PTFE sector, MRVL (DSP, Google attach, Maia 300), and the CPU supply chain (AMD)(INTC)."

However, risks include AI demand slowdown, infrastructure deployment, supply constraints and competition.

data.title: Anthropic co-founder Clark projects U.S. GDP to hit $44T by 2030 thanks to AI
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) ‌co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday that one of his company’s internal economic models projected U.S. economic output to reach $44T by 2030 thanks to fast-improving AI capabilities that could transform all fields at a more rapid pace.

He made the remarks at the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meeting taking place in Bangkok this week.

Clark called the $44T figure, which indicates a massive jump from the ⁠current U.S. economic output of little more than $30T, "sounds very outlandish,” but added that scientific discovery is expanding considerably due to AI.

"I know, ​but it's ​implicated ⁠by the technology continuing to get better. And if ​GDP were to grow this ​much, ⁠then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need ⁠to ​have been created ​to power such a major economic expansion,” he said according to Reuters.

Additionally, Clark underscored the need for international cooperation to establish "unusual and serious ​rules" for the transformative technology.

His comments echo those of Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei, who has also pushed for greater coordination among AI companies in response to fast-improving model capabilities.

In September, Amodei and other tech leaders from Google (GOOG) (GOOGL), Meta (META), SpaceX (SPCX), Nvidia (NVDA), and OpenAI (OPENAI) signed off on a White House accord that calls for responsible training and development of frontier AI models.

data.title: Brent crude hits $110 for first time since May; U.S. WTI tops $100
data.description:
Brent crude oil hit $110/bbl for the first time since May, and WTI crude rose by the largest weekly percentage since July on concerns over continued Middle East supply risks and uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as Ukraine's renewed targeting of Russian refineries.

Shipping risks remain high after two cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz following attacks this week, and risks to shipping have raised freight and insurance costs, contributing to the higher price of oil.

Ukraine reportedly struck Russia's Ryazan ⁠refinery on Thursday after President Zelenskyy declared his country was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced a week ago by President Trump.

"We're still in a bull market," BOK Financial senior VP of trading Dennis Kissler said in a note, as flows through the Strait of Hormuz are not reliable, expectations of Russian diesel coming onto the market are not being met, and with Ukrainian attacks on refineries, "those barrels are going to have trouble getting to the market."

A third factor is that demand destruction "at least in the U.S. is not happening," Kissler added, noting this week's report of surprisingly large drawdowns of U.S. fuel inventories, with distillate inventories—which include diesel and heating oil—at 102.6M barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration, down 12% Y/Y.

The U.S. Department of Energy requested an exchange of up to 17M ​barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on Friday, after previously agreeing to loan 172M barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with International Energy Agency member states to release 400M barrels from reserves around the world.

However, oil prices above $100 look increasingly stretched relative to market fundamentals, as Middle Eastern exports have largely recovered and global oil inventories remain comfortable, Julius Baer's Norbert Rucker said in a note.

Diesel supply concerns could also ease as higher product exports and reduced refinery maintenance support availability, Rucker added.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for November delivery jumped 3.5% to $101.41, its highest settlement value since September 17, and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for December delivery surged 3.7% to $109.86/bbl, its best close since May 19.

Front-month Nymex ULSD (HO1:COM) for November delivery added 1.1% on Friday to $4.8991/gal, while front-month Nymex RBOB November gasoline (XB1:COM) gained 1.7% to $3.2354/gal.

For the full week, Nymex soared 10.4%, its largest one-week percentage gain since the week ending July 17, Brent crude climbed 4.9%, its fourth consecutive weekly gain, ULSD jumped 3.4%, but RBOB fell 1.8%.

U.S. natural gas futures (NG1:COM) fell on Friday as the market appeared to look past this weekend's anticipated cold spell in the Northeast that is expected to drive up residential and commercial heating demand; the front-month Nymex November contract fell 3.7% on Friday to $3.1160/MMBtu, down 3.2% on the week.

Friday's top five stocks on the S&P 500 leaderboard belonged to the oil and gas sector: Targa Resources (TRGP) up 4.4%, Diamondback Energy up 4.3%, EOG Resources (EOG) up 4.2%, Kinder Morgan (KMI) up 4.2%, APA Corp. (APA) up 4.1%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), rose 4.8% this week.

ETFs: (USO), (BNO), (UCO), (SCO), (USL), (DBO), (DRIP), (GUSH), (USOI), (UNG), (BOIL), (KOLD), (UNL), (FCG), (XLE), (XOP)
